segments: The seventeenth discourse.
The Hunnic kings.
[... the] Jew, as prefect and ruler for two years, more or less,
and he was killed.
And because of him all the Jews throughout the inhabited world were hated and persecuted.
After Arghun son of Abaqa, [reigned] his brother Gaykhatu, who was called Nenjin Turgi. For at the beginning of his reign his brother Arghun had arranged for him
to take a myriarch of the Mongol army
and go and guard the regions of Rome (Anatolia).
And while he was there during the entire period that Arghun lived,
the places over there pleased (him?);
and he did not want to leave them again.
Until it happened that when his brother Arghun died,
and all the royal princes assembled,
and they all adjudged it right for him to sit upon the throne of the kingdom,
only with difficulty and as if by compulsion could he be drawn to sit in his brother's place.
Because in those regions of Rome (Anatolia) he lived in great ease and abundant comfort,
eating and drinking and revelling in worldly pleasures.
Especially when he saw those two kings who were before him,
that in the prime of their youth the thread of their life was cut off,
and they had not had their fill of this temporal life,
he therefore turned his back,
and did not consent to sit upon the throne of the kingdom,
and to return to the land of the Romans was his chief desire, and toward this was his longing inclined.
And thus he made an agreement,
and kept the princes and the nobles in suspense with hope,
saying that in the spring, that is, at the turn of the year, he would come and assume rule.
And he left them
and set out for the regions of the Romans (Anatolia).
And when he arrived there,
he found the Turkmen Uj (frontier) people of the house of Qaraman laying hands upon the Mongols,
taking captives, plundering, conquering, and laying waste.
Gaykhatu gathered his armies,
and went and encamped against the famous fortress of Tangazlu (Denizli);
and he took it by the sword,
and killed in it a multitude of people.
And he put to the sword the rest of the Uj people who had fled to the villages,
and devastated them exceedingly.
And because when his brother Arghun ...
Tungin.
